editorial:
Imagine being so tired of your partner that you want a divorce, but you are stuck because of a silly note you wrote while wasted years ago. That is exactly the mess Nina and Richard are in. They signed a napkin promising that whoever breaks up the relationship loses every single cent of their shared money. Now, they are trapped in a hilarious game of chicken, trying to trick the other person into being the bad guy so they can walk away rich. The vibe is light, chaotic, and feels like a giant prank that just keeps getting worse for both of them.

You will love how the actors play off each other with great timing and funny arguments. The plot moves fast, though some of the side characters feel a bit thin. If you enjoy movies about couples fighting in the funniest way possible, you need to see this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the great facial expressions, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends. It is a perfect choice for a lazy Sunday.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Nina and Richard both try to fake a huge scandal to force the other to end things. However, they accidentally discover the original napkin was signed with a pen that fades over time. Since the contract is now blank, the legal threat is gone. Instead of fighting, they realize they actually miss each other. They decide to tear up the napkin and try therapy instead of fighting over the money.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves romantic comedies with a twist.
